Professional fashion photograph, full body shot. ONE woman standing.

a warm golden-brown complexion, early 20s goddess, heavy muscle physique THE MOST EXTREME PHYSICALLY POSSIBLE beyond all anatomy limits — an enormous, overwhelmingly muscular woman; massive thick arms with heavy defined muscle, a broad powerful muscular back, a huge powerful chest, a heavy dense muscular torso and legs, only a soft hint of a waistline; enormous round hips and colossal thick thighs with muscle visible through a soft layer, thick heavy calves; not slim, not lean; her arms, hands, legs and feet stay in correct proportion to each other, shaggy layered balayage hair — her bare skin covered from the neck down in photographic film imagery: strips of film frames in orange-brown negative tones running across her torso, arms and legs, tiny sprocket holes along their edges and small frame numbers, each frame showing a tiny inverted-tone portrait or landscape, a red grease-pencil circle around a few frames, the pattern sitting in living skin and following every curve beneath it, covering all of her skin from the neck to the ankles and the backs of her hands, her face left unpainted and the pattern fading out at the neck. Jewelry: a wide gold waist chain resting over the carved curve of her hips, a pearl choker and a long strand of pearls hanging low on her chest, and a fine gold chain looped around her thigh above the knee. Jewelry is metal and pearl only, worn on the body, nothing added to her face or ears.

Background: a snow-covered stone plaza in soft daylight with light snow lying only on the ground, a fountain edge under snow, standard lamp posts and a waist-high railing, lit by natural light with soft shadows on the skin, the whole floor and surroundings clearly visible and in focus. ONE woman only. Full-length wide shot from a moderate distance with the camera at waist height, the whole figure from the soles of the boots to the top of her head completely visible, with the door, railing or steps beside her at normal human scale so the extreme heel height reads at a glance, the towering heels clearly separating the boot soles from the floor. This is one single photograph taken with one camera at one moment, shot on a medium format camera with an 85mm lens at f/5.6, realistic photographic grain, a real photograph.
